packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-06 - unverified image-only reading (first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (face 1, overview image-001.jpg)
Observation: a board of about 17 small detached paper/parchment slips laid on black, with a colour checker and a cm scale (right edge, ~4-38 cm). No complete leaf; these are strips and scraps, mostly with 2-9 short line-fragments each. Many carry modern pencil labels of the form "Stams, STA, Fag. 21-NNa" (e.g. "Fag. 21-14a", "Fag. 21-12a", "Fag. 21-6a", "Fag. 21-5a", "Fag. 21-13a", "Fag. 21-11a", "Fag. 21-1a" visible at overview scale) - these are modern shelf/label notes, not text.
Scripts: at least two hands visible at overview scale: (a) a Latin humanistic/early-modern cursive in brown ink (e.g. top-left slip "fuit sponsa parens", lower slip "animo cap(...) fuisse, et / fortem(?) .. / partem curie"); (b) a German Kurrent-type cursive on the bottom-right larger slip (Fag. 21-1a), ~7 lines. One slip (centre-left, Fag. 21-13a) has an enlarged initial P ("Petrum"). No columns, running titles, or rubrics visible; no glosses. All slips appear upright as mounted, but orientation of each is not guaranteed.
Tentative: the fragments are probably from several different documents/letters (different hands, Latin and German); I do not assume they belong together.
Tiles: image-002..010 are a 3x3 grid of native-resolution tiles over this face (rows: 002-004 top, 005-007 middle, 008-010 bottom). image-011 is the overview of a second face (probably the versos), with tiles 012-020.

=== image-002.jpg (face 1, top-left tile) ===
Contains three slips (line numbers counted from top of image, per slip in reading order):

Slip A (top-left, pencil label "Stoms(=Stams), STA, Fag. 21-14a"): ruled frame lines (vertical line at left of text, horizontal above). Paper/vellum with laid/chain lines visible. One line of text in a large humanistic cursive:
image-002 l.1: fuit Sponsa parens q(ue?)   [final "q" with a stroke/tail through descender, possibly "q(ue)" or "q(uo)"; below it at far right a small "B."-like mark - possibly a catchword/signature or a flourish]
(Text above line 1 cut away; only ascender tips remain at top edge.)

Slip B (top-right, pencil "Fag. 21-12a"): left edge torn, text is right-side portion of lines.
image-002 l.1 (top): "S J" (or "§ J") large letters, then "1?" at far right - possibly a heading or numeral; uncertain
image-002 l.2: [..]raris for[..]
image-002 l.3: [..]te muitas(?) / mutat(?)[..]   [reads "te muitas"/"te muita"; uncertain - could be "te mutat" or "re ruitas"]
image-002 l.4: [..]l laudes[..]   [or "laudib(us)"; final letter has a curl, possibly "laudes" or "laudi(bus)"]
image-002 l.5: [..]L(?)espi[..]  [very uncertain]

Slip C (bottom right, partly cut by tile edge; small torn scrap above slip D): large cursive letters, orientation unclear (may be upside down or a flourished heading). Unreadable as words at this scale: [illegible] - see tile image-005 for the rest.
Slip D (bottom right edge): first line "[..]ecubue" (cf. overview "...ecubue"); continued on image-005.

=== image-003.jpg (face 1, top-centre tile) ===
Overlap: left edge repeats Slip B (Fag. 21-12a) and the bottom-left repeats slips C/D of image-002; not re-read as new text.

Slip E (top right, pencil "Stams, STA / Fag. 21-6a"): left edge cut (line beginnings lost), right edge cut. Humanistic cursive, same style as slip A (long s, "et"-type ligatures). Six lines:
image-003 l.1: [..]um famul[..]   [famuli/famulis?]
image-003 l.2: [..]ant(?) | quod statim[..]   [a heavy vertical stroke between "ant" and "quod" - possibly a long descender from the line above, or a strike; "ant" may be the end of a word with a q-like hook "antq(ue)?"]
image-003 l.3: [..]t nihil(?) continebat[..]   ["nihil" uncertain: letters u/n-i-h-i-l with an ascender loop above; "continebat" clear, may continue "continebant"]
image-003 l.4: [..]ligentio(?) uerum[..]   [first word ends "-gentio" or "-gentia"; could be "[di]ligentia"; "uerum" or "ueram"]
image-003 l.5: [..]it me omnem[..]
image-003 l.6: ad uos quam
(right margin, level of l.7: a descender/long stroke "J" - possibly start of a further line)

Slip F (bottom centre, pencil "Fag. 21-11a"): large flourished pen strokes: a looped ascender at top; then horizontal bars "C[..]rr" with a long sweeping stroke; then "S" / "Dee(?)" with a strike-through-like horizontal; at bottom "[..]ang(?)". These look like large display letters, a signature-type flourish, or pen trials, not running text. Readings: [illegible flourished letters]; possibly "Sum[..]" / "Dur[..]". I do not trust any word reading on this slip.

=== image-004.jpg (face 1, top-right tile) ===
Overlap: left edge repeats Slip E (Fag. 21-6a) from image-003; no new text there.

Slip G (centre, pencil "Fag. 21-5a"): small rectangle, cut on all sides. Mixed sizes; a long horizontal pen line runs across under l.3 (rule or a stroke). Lines:
image-004 l.1: [..]oficis(c?)cio  Vale[..]   [first word could be "[pr]oficiscio(r?)" - letters "oficis" then a c-like stroke and "cio"; "Vale" in larger letters, may be "Vale[..]" the farewell formula or a name]
image-004 l.2: [..] , ae(?) 2[..]   [faint small writing at right: "ae 22"? uncertain]
image-004 l.3: [..]noss(?) rec(?)[..]   [heavy, partly crossed by the horizontal line; letters "no" + two long s + "re" with a mark above; could be "nosse" or a deleted word]
image-004 l.4: Argumen[..]   [smaller letters, right half; "Argumen(tum)?"]
image-004 l.5: hem(?)   a[..]   [first word "hem"/"herr"/"hen"; uncertain]
image-004 l.6: [..]nus(?) meus inuitatu[..]   [lowest line, cut by bottom edge; "meus" clear, "inuitatu(s)" fairly likely (minims ambiguous: "imitatu"? ); first word "[..]rnus"/"[..]enus"]

Slip H (bottom right, pencil "Fag. 21-4a"): small scrap, script looks like a German current hand (Kurrent-type e and h); possibly German text. Lines:
image-004 l.1: [..]m  [..]   [top, mostly cut]
image-004 l.2: [..]albn(?) mit(?)[..]   [or "albu nik"; uncertain]
image-004 l.3: [..]f in bitten(?)[..]   ["bitten"/"bittn" plausible]
image-004 l.4: [..]nt auf hal[..]   ["auf" fairly clear; "hal[..]" ]

=== image-005.jpg (face 1, middle-left tile) ===
Slip C (top right, small scrap above slip D): large cursive letters, likely mounted rotated or upside down (letter shapes do not read upright). Visible forms: "sus"(?), "P[..]", "Je[..]", "go"(?) - [illegible as text]. Same scrap as at bottom of image-002 (overlap).

Slip D (pencil "Stams, STA, Fag. 21-13a"): narrow vertical strip, left side torn so line beginnings are lost; right edge appears to be the original line end (lines end with whole words). Humanistic cursive. Enlarged initial P (darker ink, like a display capital) on l.3.
image-005 l.1: [..]ea(?) ocubue   [first letters partly lost/struck; "ocubue" or "acubue" - word continues on next line? I do not supply]
image-005 l.2: [..]nt famulus
image-005 l.3: [..]ses, Petru(m)   [macron over u; a small superscript s-like mark above "u" too; "P" is the enlarged initial]
image-005 l.4: [..]qui eum ad
image-005 l.5: [..]Tuehtre(?)   [capital T or "Tu"; reads "Tuehtre"/"Tuchtre"/"Tuelitre" - perhaps a proper name; uncertain]
image-005 l.6: [..] querenam(?)   ["quaerenam"? or "quereram"; uncertain whether n or r]
image-005 l.7: [..]nis mihi·   [with a point after]
image-005 l.8: [..]tiam ad
image-005 l.9: [..]miam   [or "[..]nnam"; first letter cut]
(No text below l.9; pencil label follows.)

Slip I (bottom, pencil label on it elsewhere; numeral "12" at left edge): see image-008 for full reading. Visible here: "12  [..]e(?)  P[..] / Su[..]"

=== image-006.jpg (face 1, middle-centre tile) ===
Overlap: left edge repeats slips C and D (Fag. 21-13a); top-centre repeats lower half of Slip F (Fag. 21-11a, flourishes, bottom shows "[..]ang(?)" / "[..]any"); no new readable text there. Bottom edge shows top of Slip I (pencil "Fag. 21-9a"), read on image-008/009. Right edge shows left part of Slip K, read on image-007.

Slip J (centre, pencil "Fag. 21-10a"): small square scrap, German current hand (Kurrent-type h and long s/ch); cut on all sides.
image-006 l.1: [..]hab dis(?)g[..]   ["hab" fairly clear; next word "dis/diß" + "g" or "gn"; uncertain]
image-006 l.2: [..]ich gern(?)[..]   ["ich" fairly clear; "garn/gern/gann" uncertain]

=== image-007.jpg (face 1, middle-right tile) ===
Overlap: top-right repeats Slip H (Fag. 21-4a) from image-004; no new text.

Slip K (left, pencil "Fag. 21-7a"): horizontal strip, cut left and right; top line cut through the middle of the letters. Crop: crop-01.jpg (2x enlargement).
image-007 l.1: [..]ua(?) habente(?) de reg(?)[..]   [lower halves of letters only; "habente/lubente" and "de" plausible; last word "reg.."/"rege.."; very uncertain]
image-007 l.2: [..]1 • p(r)axime(?) quia sic libr[..]   [a large dot (paragraph/punctus) before the word; first letter p with a circumflex-like mark over the following "r"/"a"; I read "praxime" - "proxime" not excluded; "quia sic libr[..]" clear]
image-007 l.3: [..]  Qu(?)  ..  a(?) [..]   [tops of letters only; illegible]

Slip M (centre, pencil "Fag. 21-3a"): wedge-shaped scrap; only line beginnings (left side) or line ends preserved - left edge seems to be text start. Hand like slips A/E.
image-007 l.1: r[..]
image-007 l.2: m[..]   [or "nu"]
image-007 l.3: sta[..]
image-007 l.4: nos ·o·(?)   [after "nos" a mark like "o" or a punctuation sign]
image-007 l.5: suas attu[..]   ["attu[lit]"? not supplied]
image-007 l.6: De(?) mee(?) n[..]   [first letter large looped D or S; "mee"/"nec"; uncertain]
image-007 l.7: [..]ofus(?)/"[..]esus(?)" [..]   [bottom, cut; uncertain]

Slip L (right edge, pencil "STA, Fag. 21-2a", written vertically): vertical strip, line beginnings preserved (left edge); German current hand, heavier, brown staining at top. Continues on image-010.
image-007 l.1: J13(?) / "Js"(?)   [heading-like large letters, possibly "Ʒ13" or a flourished "Jt(em)"; uncertain]
image-007 l.2: Argum[..]   [or "Argem"]
image-007 l.3: Untung(?)/"Vntung"[..]   ["Vnt.." clear-ish]
image-007 l.4: 3 and[..] / "Zand"[..]   [uncertain]
image-007 l.5: Din w[..]   [or "Dir u"/"Den w"]
image-007 l.6: Pan(?)s/"Vans"[..]
image-007 l.7: Ein wi[..]   [or "Cin w"]
image-007 l.8: P(un)?l[..] / "Penne"(?)   [cut by tile edge; see image-010]

=== image-008.jpg (face 1, bottom-left tile) ===
Only the left ends of two slips; main reading on image-009.
Slip I left piece (two joined pieces; German current hand, faded brown): 
image-008 l.1: 12. | gelesen(?)  D[..]   ["12." numeral at the start, then a vertical stroke (frame/ruling?); "geles(e)n"/"gelopn" uncertain]
image-008 l.2: [..]en benoß(?) wys(?) [..]   [faint; "fu(r) b(e)no.." uncertain; illegible in part]
Slip N (bottom right corner, pencil "Fag. 21[..]"): only first letters "a[..]", "f[..]", "f[..]/b[..]" visible; read on image-009.

=== image-009.jpg (face 1, bottom-centre tile) ===
Slip I (top, pencil "Fag. 21-9a"; joined to the left piece seen on image-008; a tear/notch between pieces): German current hand, two lines (plus ascender tips of a line above). Right end is a line end (period after "hat").
image-009 l.1: [..]gelesen(?) D[..]ar(?) fenglich(?) Dannihin(?) was   ["fenglich/fünglich" fairly clear; "Dan.." word could be "Dannisin/Daniesen/Damihin"; final word "was" with long s]
image-009 l.2: [..]ns(?) wys(?) [tear] in nit gefu(n)den hat.   ["nit" clear; "gefūden" with a mark over u (nasal bar or u-diacritic) = "gefunden"; "hat." clear with point]
(Joined reading with image-008: "12. | gelesen(?) D[..]ar fenglich Dannihin(?) was / [..]en benoß(?) wys [..]in nit gefunden hat." - left piece faint, keep uncertain.)

Slip N (bottom, pencil "Fag. 21-8a"): Latin, humanistic cursive; three lines; left and right edges cut; a hole between "c" and "bra" in l.2 and in "conte" in l.3.
image-009 l.1: animo cap[..]s(?) fuisse, et   ["capt9"? - the word is "cap" + a looped abbreviation/letters "ts"; "captus" plausible but not certain; comma after "fuisse"]
image-009 l.2: fortem(?) fustib(us) c[hole]bra[..]   [first letter long s/f-shaped: "fortem" or "sortem"; "fustibus" with the -us sign (9/y-shape) after "fustib"; then "c" + hole + "bra"]
image-009 l.3: partem curie conte[..]   ["curie" = curiae; "conte"/"contente"/"contentu" uncertain; hole through the middle]
Slip O (bottom right edge, pencil "Fag. 21-1a"): only the left margin visible here; read on image-010.

=== image-010.jpg (face 1, bottom-right tile) ===
Overlap: top-left repeats bottom of Slip M (Fag. 21-3a: "De(?) mee n[..]", "[..]ofus(?)"); top-right repeats lower Slip L (Fag. 21-2a).
Slip L continued (lines after image-007 l.7, line beginnings only, German current hand):
image-010 l.1: Din w[..]   (= image-007 l.5, overlap)
image-010 l.2: Pans(?)[..]   (= image-007 l.6)
image-010 l.3: Ein wi[..]   (= image-007 l.7)
image-010 l.4: Pun(?)h(?)[..] / "Rüml"(?)   [large looped initial; uncertain]
image-010 l.5: Def(?)/"Doß"[..]   [uncertain]
image-010 l.6: Ve(?)[..] / "Vn"   [uncertain; torn below]

Slip O (bottom, pencil "Fag. 21-1a"): the largest slip; German current (Kurrent) hand, brown ink, 6 lines plus descender tips of a 7th; left edge cut (but lines 2-6 seem to start near the left margin), right edge cut; two holes at lower left and lower centre. Long looped ascenders/descenders cross into adjacent lines. Crop: crop-02.jpg (1.4x).
image-010 l.1: [..]ehen(?) lasse. Der rat(?) hat etlichen(?) den(?)   ["lasse." with point; "Der" clear; "rat/rot/vot" - the r is the Kurrent x-like r; "hat" clear; "etlichen/etlichē" probable; last word "den/dem/deu"]
image-010 l.2: lanz(?) knechten den lon gadopl(?) • Nicolau[..]   ["lanz"/"lang" + "knechten" (k with loop, "-echten"); "den lon" fairly clear (= den Lohn?); "gadopl"/"gedopl" uncertain; a heavy dot, then "Nicolau(s)" or "Nicolaus" - capital N; cut at right]
image-010 l.3: hat den gartten(?) dem ischuhen(?) verkauft hab(?)[..]   ["hat den" clear; "gartten" (double t) probable; "dem" + word "ischuhen/ischuhn/Schuhen" uncertain; "verkauft" fairly clear; last "hab/hat" cut]
image-010 l.4: mit mine(r?) maut(?) mul(?) haben. Ich hab   ["mit" clear; next "mine/nimer/mme"; "maut/mart" with a mark (u-hook) over u; "mul/mit/auf"? before "haben."; "Ich hab" clear]
image-010 l.5: inhend(?) widem(?) rate(?) [hole] eben(?) vergebung(?) im   [very uncertain word divisions; "vergebung/verjehung/versehung" - first letters "ver" probable; "im/um" at end]
image-010 l.6: [..]isp(r)echen(?) laidt. Darum(?) [hole] nit mit stoltheit(?)[..]   ["laidt." (= leid?) with point; "nit" clear; "stoltheit"/"stolthaite" probable but uncertain]
image-010 l.7: [descender tips only; illegible]

LAYOUT SURVEY (face 2, overview image-011.jpg)
